claims.text: Structural metallic alloys conventionally exhibit a trade-off between high strength and good ductility.
A machine-learning model can integrate experimental datasets and simulation results.
The integrated machine-learning model can predict processing conditions that produce a refined grain structure.
The integrated machine-learning model can predict processing conditions that produce a tailored precipitate distribution.
A microstructure combining refined grains with a tailored precipitate distribution can concurrently improve strength and ductility.
An ML framework can identify optimized thermal and mechanical treatment parameters from integrated historical experimental and simulation data.
Implementing ML-optimized processing conditions will create a microstructure with refined grains and a controlled, synergistic precipitate distribution.
Refined grains enhance yield strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Effective precipitate dispersion enhances yield strength.
A beneficial balance of phase distribution helps maintain or improve ductility.
Mitigation of stress-concentration sites helps maintain or improve ductility.
ML-optimized specimens will have higher yield strength than conventionally processed specimens.
ML-optimized specimens will retain or improve ductility relative to conventionally processed specimens.
Traditional alloying, conventional precipitation hardening, and severe grain refinement typically improve one of strength or ductility at the expense of the other.
The effectiveness of the ML approach is limited by the quality and diversity of its input datasets.
The ML approach is primarily applicable within the processing-parameter range represented reliably in the training data.
Noise and bias in historical data may affect the ML model's predictions.
